title: No-Code Tools vs Hiring a Developer: What Fits Your Project?
h1: No-code tools vs hiring a developer: what fits your project?
description: No-code platforms and custom development compared: speed, cost, flexibility, scale, ownership and when to build with tools or hire a developer.
intro: No-code tools let you build websites, forms, simple apps and automations by dragging and connecting blocks. Developers write custom code. Each approach has real strengths. This article explains when no-code is enough, when custom development is worth the cost and how a freelancer can help in either case.

faq.q: Can I start with no-code and move to code later?
faq.a: Yes. Many products begin as no-code prototypes, then move to custom code when they need more control or scale.

faq.q: Is no-code only for simple projects?
faq.a: Not only, but there are limits. Unusual logic, heavy traffic or special integrations may need custom work.
Check the terms. With no-code you depend on the platform, while custom code is usually yours.

faq.q: Do I still need a freelancer for no-code?
faq.a: Often yes, for setup, design and connecting tools, especially if you are short on time.
Write down what the product must do and what could go wrong if the platform changes or limits you.
